patch_description: Crossover of the two top-performing variants. From the inspiration program I take the widen-only innovation-adaptive measurement noise (R[k] = max(R0, 0.7*R0 + 0.3*ewma_var)) stored in an Rseq that is also reused in the second iterated RTS refinement pass — this variant measured slightly better slope_changes (29.2 vs 31.6) and false_reversals (23.0 vs 24.4) while keeping responsiveness identical. From the current program I keep the improved ripple damper: the lower alpha floor (0.40), the cascade of two moderate bilateral one-pole passes (alpha=0.65) instead of one aggressive pass when heavy suppression is requested (flatter group-delay profile, better smoothness without lag), and the correlation guard that backs alpha off toward 0.85 if the damper distorts the trajectory (protects tracking accuracy). This combines the better noise-adaptation of the inspiration with the better zero-phase damping of the current program, keeping the same I/O contract.
